tools.name: intent_publish_intent
tools.description: Use this when the user asks AutoIsto to keep watching Czech car listings for them over time (e.g. "let me know until March about an estate car under 300 000 CZK, not diesel"). This does NOT start watching by itself and takes no e-mail address or other personal data: it returns a consentUrl on www.au

tools.name: intent_get_intent
tools.description: Use this to check whether an intent created with intent_publish_intent is already confirmed by the user and active, waiting, expired or withdrawn. Requires the intentCode; returns the statement and dates only — never the user's e-mail, the hidden limit or any other personal data.

tools.name: intent_list_matches
tools.description: Use this when the user asks what AutoIsto has found for an intent created with intent_publish_intent. These are the same cars AutoIsto e-mails to the user; this server cannot send messages into the conversation by itself. Requires the intentCode; optional since (ISO time) returns only newer matches.

tools.name: intent_withdraw_intent
tools.description: Use this when the user wants AutoIsto to stop watching for an intent created with intent_publish_intent. Takes effect immediately; nothing more is e-mailed for it. Requires the intentCode.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "zamery" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: intent_list_matches · Public sink: intent_publish_intent, intent_list_matches.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: intent_list_matches · Public sink: intent_publish_intent, intent_list_matches

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
